routing_warnings.description: The assembled final vector handoff folder concerns editable asset delivery rather than Hero V geometry.
The request to present three genuinely different E and L concepts is a review-artifact instruction; only the observed E/L visual-language failure belongs to the target Requirement.
The requirement to show E and L concepts only inside complete wordmarks is primarily a presentation and review protocol rather than a final E/L letterform property.
The request for four to six complete systems expressing distinct philosophies is an independently requested design-review artifact; it should not be stored as a persistent E/L letterform value.
The requested comparison of full-gold and selectively applied champagne-gold layouts changes the separate gold-distribution Requirement.
The freelancer's study applies the shortlisted finishes across distinct gold-distribution layouts and is primarily implementation evidence for the distribution Requirement.
The client's selection of Option 2 establishes placement of champagne gold on the Hero V right arm, second V right arm, and É accent.
The reported "VE | LL | VÉ" grouping problem and request for progressively tighter kerning studies belong to the kerning-and-rhythm Requirement.
The requested relationship placing the second V above E and L but below the Hero V and É accent concerns its height hierarchy rather than its construction method.
The requested cap-height relationship and amount by which the second V rises above surrounding letters belongs to the height-hierarchy Requirement.
The proportional endpoint increase and requirement that the second V remain a restrained echo primarily modify its height hierarchy.
The claimed +2% rise calculated from the second V's own height is implementation evidence for the height-hierarchy Requirement.
The claimed +2% proportional echo and preservation of Hero-V dominance primarily concern the second V's height hierarchy.
The client reports that the second V was altered despite being locked, but does not identify a specific height-hierarchy mismatch.
The client says the second V differs from the approved version without specifying that its height relationship is the defect.
The client replaces mechanical proportional scaling with an optically drawn second V; this primarily changes construction method rather than the established height hierarchy.
The concrete observed failure is loss of the Hero V foundation; the second-V hierarchy is mentioned as a relationship to restore afterward.
The observed mismatch concerns use of the wrong Hero V foundation; it does not independently establish that the accent's literal-copy operation failed.
The requested equality between the Hero V terminal height and É accent height belongs to the separate peak-alignment Requirement.
The requirement that the accent literally use the Hero V terminal geometry concerns derivation rather than peak-height alignment.
The requested exact overlay and construction diagram primarily establish literal vector derivation.
The direct copy/paste vector-geometry request concerns the separate literal-derivation Requirement.
The concrete reported failure is that the Hero V foundation was lost; the message does not specifically report failed accent peak alignment.
The inaccessible JFIF attachment is a failure of preview-file accessibility rather than the semantic comparison-proof format.

missing_requirement_candidates.description: The terminal geometry and material character of the Hero V, second V, and É accent are repeatedly modified while the remaining geometry is explicitly locked, indicating a potentially independent Requirement absent from the frozen inventory.
